To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) detailed information about COVID-19 vaccines, including information about the results of clinical trials of the vaccine, does not reduce intentions of the public to receive a COVID-19 vaccine, and 2) detailed information about the effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines and the need to continue to engage in protective behaviour post vaccination does not reduce intentions in the public to receive the vaccine or reduce the perceived effectiveness of the vaccine.
transparent information about COVID  19 vaccination effectiveness and side effects does not have a negative effect on intentions to be vaccinated or on protective behaviours.

the effects of transparent communication about COVID 19 vaccination on behavioural intentions.
the potential for transparent communication of the limitations of vaccines to reduce vaccine hesitancy and increase protective behaviours.
the communication of uncertainty about vaccine effectiveness and side effects.

there is no evidence that transparently communicating about the limitations of vaccines has a negative impact on intentions to receive the vaccine.
transparent communication about vaccine efficacy and side effects does not have a negative effect on intentions to receive the vaccine.
the results of this study suggest that providing transparent and comprehensive information about COVID 9 vaccinations does not reduce people's intentions to receive a vaccination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results are consistent with the idea that people have an intuitive understanding of the limitations of vaccines, and are not swayed by transparent communications about these.

the results are consistent with a view that people are not overly influenced by information that is transparent about the uncertainty surrounding the effectiveness of the vaccine and the need to continue to engage in protective behaviour post vaccination.

people do not seem to change their behaviour based on the information they are given about COVID 19 vaccinations.
